- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in 1–3 day horizon.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in 10–14 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3%.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2–6% when sentiment is flat or mildly negative; add 2–4% to forecast to compensate.
- If sentiment history shows recent negative spikes (e.g., -1.00), model tends to lag in correction; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce by 3–5%.
- When sentiment is positive but recent price is falling, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–4% in 5–10 day horizon to avoid overbought bias.
